title: TED:Text-Axis Evidence Decomposition for Prompted Anomaly Localization
abstract: arXiv:2609.39033v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: CLIP is a powerful vision-language model, but it was not designed for fine-grained defect localization; CLIP-based anomaly detectors therefore adapt it with prompts or lightweight modules to increase defect sensitivity. We show that stronger sensitivity does not necessarily make local evidence reliable: under domain shift, adapted CLIP-AD models often assign high anomaly scores to both true defects and visually complex normal regions. The issue is not simply missing defect information, but a local scoring rule that decodes defect and hard-normal evidence, having the same anomaly evidence. We propose TED (Text-Axis Evidence Decomposition), a post-hoc scoring method that asks whether each ambiguous response is better supported by source defect patches or by source normal patches mistaken as anomalous. translated_title: TED：面向提示异常定位的文本轴证据分解
translated_abstract: CLIP 是一个强大的视觉-语言模型，但它并非为细粒度缺陷定位而设计；因此，基于 CLIP 的异常检测器通过提示或轻量级模块对其进行适配，以提高缺陷敏感度。我们表明，更强的敏感度并不一定能使局部证据变得可靠：在域偏移下，经过适配的 CLIP-AD 模型往往对真实缺陷和视觉上复杂的正常区域都赋予较高的异常分数。问题并非简单地缺失缺陷信息，而在于局部评分规则会将缺陷证据与“难样本”正常证据解码为相同的异常证据。我们提出 TED（文本轴证据分解，Text-Axis Evidence Decomposition），这是一种事后评分方法，它询问每个模糊的响应是更能被源缺陷补丁所支持，还是更能被被误判为异常的源正常补丁所支持。TED 在宿主模型的“正常-异常”文本响应下比较这些支持，保持主干网络和提示不变，并且只需要（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出TED，一种即插即用的事后评分方法，通过在文本轴上比较真实缺陷补丁与被误判为异常的难正常补丁的证据支持，解决CLIP-AD模型在域偏移下将视觉复杂的正常区域误判为缺陷的问题。
en_tdlr: TED is a post-hoc scoring method that decomposes evidence along the text axis to determine whether ambiguous responses are better supported by source defect patches or by hard-normal patches mistaken as anomalous, improving the reliability of CLIP-based anomaly localization under domain shift without modifying the backbone or prompts.
